Level 1 · Introduction · Week 5

Messages and My Blocks

Break big programs into named parts.

What you will learn

  • How to break a big job into smaller named parts (decomposition).
  • How to make your own block with My Blocks, and give it an input.
  • How sprites send each other messages with broadcast.
  • How to pick colors and text that everyone can see.

The big idea

Big jobs, small named parts

A garden picture is a big job. Break it into parts and give each part a name. Then the main plan is short and easy to read.

In Scratch, My Blocks → Make a Block lets you make a pink block with your own name. You put its steps under a define hat. An input is a blank you fill in each time you use the block, like “size”.

Messages

broadcast sends a message to every sprite, like an announcement on a loudspeaker. Only scripts that start with when I receive that exact message run.

Exercise5.1: Shape Machine

Make your own block that can draw any shape.

  1. New project. Add the Pen extension. Set the cat’s Size to 40.

  2. My Blocks → Make a Block. Type polygon. Click Add an input (number or text), type sides. Add another input: length. Click OK.

  3. Build the define script. Drag the sides and length ovals out of the define hat into the slots.

  4. Build the green-flag script with your new pink block. Click the flag!

  5. Add a pentagon: one more block, “polygon 5 70”.

How many blocks would you need to draw these 4 shapes without your My Block? (blank to fill in)

Exercise5.2: Stamp Garden

  1. New project with the Pen extension. Delete the cat. Hover over Choose a Sprite and click the Paint brush. Draw a flower in the middle of the canvas (circles for the center and petals). Name the sprite Flower.

  2. Make two My Blocks: flower with an input size, and grass with no input.

  3. Build the three scripts. For the grass color, click the color circle and set Color 45, Saturation 100, Brightness 62 (see the color-safe paint box).

Done when: each click on the flag grows a new garden: a strip of grass and 12 flowers of different sizes and colors in surprise places.

Exercise5.3: Show Time

Two sprites put on a show by sending messages.

  1. New project. Keep the cat (the Presenter). Add a Dancer: any sprite with several costumes, like Ballerina.

  2. To make a message: in a “broadcast” block, click the dropdown → New message, type start show. Make another called finale.

  3. Build the scripts. Click the flag and enjoy the show!

Presenter (cat) Dancer

Bug hunt! Ada’s dancer starts with “when I receive show start”. Try it. What happens? Why? How do you fix it?

SafetyColor-safe paint box

Some people see colors differently. These colors stay different for almost everyone. In Scratch, click a color circle and type the three numbers. And never use color as the only clue: add a shape, a pattern or a word too, and keep text big.

Color Col. Sat. Bri. Color Col. Sat. Bri.
Orange 12 100 90 Blue 56 100 70
Sky blue 56 63 91 Vermillion 7 100 84
Bluish green 45 100 62 Reddish purple 91 41 80
Yellow 16 72 94 Black 0 0 0

Reflect

Why is “polygon 6 60” easier to read than the blocks inside it?

What did you do to make your project easier for everyone to see?

New words

decomposition
Breaking a big problem into smaller parts.
My Block
A block you make yourself, with a name you choose.
define
The hat block that holds the steps of your My Block.
input
A blank in a block that you fill in each time, like “size”.
broadcast
Send a message to every sprite.
when I receive
A hat block that runs when its exact message is sent.
accessible
Easy for everyone to use, including people who see or hear differently.

Homework: Messages and My Blocks

15–20 minutes. Do Core first; Challenge and Creative are optional.

CoreStarry Sky (Scratch, about 10 minutes)

Make your own “star” block and fill the night sky.

  1. Open Scratch and add the Pen extension. Pick a dark backdrop (for example Stars, or paint the backdrop dark blue).

  2. My Blocks → Make a Block: name it star, add an input size, click OK.

  3. Build both scripts. Drag size out of the define hat into the move block. For the pen color, click the color circle and set Color 16, Saturation 72, Brightness 94 (yellow from the color-safe paint box).

  4. Click the flag. Save as starry-sky.

Why does the star block turn 144 degrees and not 72? (Hint: count how many times the pen goes all the way round.)

ChallengeAdd a moon (decomposition)

Make a second My Block called moon with no input. It should go to the top-left corner and draw a big circle: repeat 36, move 8, turn 10. Use it in your green-flag script before the stars. Now your main script reads like a plan: erase all, moon, stars. Write your main script as a plan, one line per block:

CreativeGood night message

Add a Button sprite (any sprite) that says “Click me for night time”. When it is clicked, it broadcasts a new message night falls. Give the cat a “when I receive night falls” script that says “Good night!”. Check that both blocks use exactly the same message.

Self-checkSelf-check: tick each box when it is true
